data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single domain expert is more reliable than a checklist-driven panel because complex, objectively verifiable tasks often require 'gestalt' pattern recognition that cannot be decomposed into a linear checklist without losing critical contextual dependencies.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is purely additive/omission-based (e.g., a pre-flight checklist).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The domain expert is suffering from cognitive overload or extreme fatigue.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition functions as a high-dimensional heuristic that integrates non-linear variables; checklists force a reduction to one-dimensional binary checks, creating 'blind spots' where the panel satisfies all criteria but misses the emergent failure mode that an expert recognizes instantly.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
